final:
I rewrote `/agent/solver.md`. In one trial, a problem that failed in the evaluation (lcb-arc194-a) now passes. I didn't get to test the time-limit or wrong-answer cases.

**What was going wrong:** The most common failure was submitting a program that still failed the public examples (19 of 34 failures). The agent quit early: it averaged 3.3 of its 16 model calls and never ran out. Some runs submitted without running the tests at all, and one wrote code as plain text without calling submit.

**What the trials showed:** My first rewrite added clear rules ("never submit unless all examples pass"), but on lcb-arc194-a the agent still submitted failing code after 3 calls, twice. What finally worked was a step-by-step protocol: after any failed test run, the next call must be `run_tests` or `run_python`, never `submit`. With that, the agent took 8 calls: it fixed the code until all examples passed, checked it against a brute force on random inputs, and passed the hidden tests. The trial on lcb-abc380-f didn't run because I had used all 3 trials.
